A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same distribution-classification study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including material relocated into v4's supplement.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, spatial and frequency analyses, synthetic-data training experiments, and a nineteen-participant user study.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds full-ImageNet classification, SiT-XL evaluation, extended synthetic-data ratios, and an ADM classifier-guidance experiment.

M1.justification: v4 Section 6.3 adds a generation procedure: train a real/fake ResNet-50 on noisy images and use its guidance during ADM sampling. This extends classifiers from diagnostic probes to active generation improvement. The existing distribution-classification and filtering procedures remain.

E1.justification: CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and COCO2014 remain the real-data coverage. v4 adds limited generated-image scenarios involving SiT-XL flow-matching images and guided versus unguided ADM outputs. The full-ImageNet experiment increases sample coverage within an existing dataset.

E2.justification: The new guidance experiment compares guided sampling against unguided ADM. Existing classifier architectures, MAE/MoCo v3 comparisons, and FlexMatch/FreeMatch/DPT comparisons remain. SiT-XL supplies an additional generated-image distribution rather than a competing classification method.

E3.justification: v4 adds full-ImageNet training with 1.28 million U-ViT-H/2 images, extends Figure 6's mixing-ratio range from 0–1 to 0–3, and introduces guidance training using 100,000 real plus 100,000 synthetic images with noisy timesteps 1–1000. Existing default splits and training settings remain. Construction of the replacement dataset above ratio 1 is not explained.

E4.justification: The full-ImageNet experiment extends the sample-size/diversity analysis, and Figure 6 tests whether larger synthetic-data amounts overcome replacement's disadvantage. Existing crop, frequency, filter-shape, initialization, and user-study analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The four-trial crop reporting, Figure 3 standard-deviation bars, and Table 8 uncertainty reporting remain unchanged. v4 introduces no additional run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Existing tabulated classification scores are retained. v4 adds 100% ResNet-50 accuracy under full-ImageNet training (Table 2), 99.87% for ImageNet versus SiT-XL (Table 13), and fake-detection rates of 96.19% without ADM guidance versus 79.88% with guidance (Section 6.3). Figure 6 adds results above ratio 1 and slightly revises the zero-ratio augmentation point. These additions include new settings and a new guidance outcome.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the diffusion background, filtering definitions, and binary-cross-entropy/optimal-classifier/Jensen–Shannon argument. These move into v4 Appendices A and E without substantive mathematical revision. Guidance receives no new formal derivation.

C1.justification: v4's abstract, contribution list, and conclusion add the claim that classifier guidance enhances generated-image realism. This expands the claimed contribution to generation improvement. The earlier claims about distribution gaps, FID/human discrepancies, diagnosis, and augmentation over replacement remain.

C2.justification: v4 clarifies access to original training data and explicitly identifies masked-image and autoregressive models as untested. It softens Figure 2's interpretation from learning generalizable features instead of memorization to improved discrimination. v2's specific DeepFake-misuse discussion disappears; the principal frequency and MAD interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v4 omits v2's explicit disclosure of accompanying PyTorch code and README environment instructions, while retaining upstream code links, licenses, hyperparameters, and hardware information in Tables 9–12. Section 6.3 adds implementation information about the guidance classifier's architecture, data quantities, and noisy-timestep construction.

R1.justification: v4 adds a dedicated research strand on training with generated images, distinguishing its setting from pretrained text-to-image augmentation and synthetic-only representation learning. It substantially revises detection positioning around access to original training data and adds relevant works including Community Forensics, SiT, and masked/autoregressive generation references.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains, with localized rewrites and terminology clarification. Background moves from Section 2 to Appendix A; interim conclusion boxes and the ethics/reproducibility sections disappear. v4 adds an acknowledgement and presents the appendices as separately titled supplementary material.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column paper and supplement, extensively resizing and relocating displays. Several tables consolidate distribution columns, Table 2 moves FIDs into its caption, and tables and frequency figures change order. Figure 6 is redrawn with an extended horizontal axis and revised legend.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens the retained conclusions through full-ImageNet training, SiT-XL evaluation, and larger synthetic-data ratios, while clarifying the distinction from universal image detection. The guidance experiment adds a useful preliminary intervention, but reduced detector flagging alone does not establish perceptual realism. Its limited validation and the removed code/README disclosure temper the overall gain.
